case_title: Raju Gupta S/o Sh. Madan Mohan Gupta vs Manoj Kumar and Others
court: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Pilot Court), Karkardooma Courts, Delhi

respondents: Manoj Kumar S/o Sh. Babu Ram (driver)
Ram Singh S/o Sh. G.S. Meena (owner)
claimants: Raju Gupta S/o Sh. Madan Mohan Gupta
Satish Kumar S/o Sh. Kanhaiya Lal

core_facts: On 14/15.02.2016 at about 2 AM, all three petitioners boarded auto-rickshaw DL 1 RM 0893 at Khajuri Chowk to go to Sonia Vihar; driver drove rashly at high speed and collided with stationary truck HR 55F 2507 at Wazirabad Road in front of Sonia Vihar Water Plant
FIR No. 155/16 was registered at PS Kajoori Khas under Sections 279/337/338 IPC; respondents were common across all three petitions
Raju Gupta (DAR 153/16) sustained 37% physical disability in left lower limb and right upper limb; functional disability assessed at 20% of the whole body
Income assessed at minimum wages for unskilled workman on 15.02.2016 at Rs. 9,178 per month; no future prospects addition per Pranay Sethi judgment
Neelam (DAR 154/16) and Satish Kumar (DAR 155/16) sustained simple injuries only; no significant loss of income or disability established
National Insurance Co. held liable under a valid policy (No. 361801/31/14/670000152) covering the offending auto for the period 10.03.2015 to 09.03.2016
legal_issues: Whether rash and negligent driving by the auto driver was established as the cause of the collision
Quantum of compensation for Raju Gupta with 37% physical and 20% functional disability
Whether future prospects are to be added when income is assessed at minimum wages
Liability of National Insurance Co. under the policy
outcome: All three petitions allowed. Raju Gupta (DAR 153/16) awarded Rs. 5,33,033 (primarily Rs. 3,52,432 for future loss of income at 20% functional disability, multiplier 16, plus wages for 5 months, pain and suffering, amenities, attendant charges, and medical expenses). Neelam (DAR 154/16) and Satish Kumar (DAR 155/16) each awarded Rs. 15,000 for simple injuries. National Insurance Co. directed to pay all amounts with 9% interest from date of filing.
key_holdings: Negligence of the driver is established through FIR, site plan, and eyewitness evidence on preponderance of probability; denial without counter-evidence is insufficient to rebut the claim.

Functional disability for compensation purposes is assessed as a percentage of the whole body even where the physical disability certificate specifies injury to a particular limb, following Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343.
Future prospects cannot be added to income assessed at statutory minimum wages where the petitioner has not proved a fixed salary or regular employment.

summary: This common award disposed of three DAR petitions (153/16, 154/16, 155/16) before the MACT, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi. On 14-15 February 2016 at 2 AM, the three petitioners—Raju Gupta, Neelam, and Satish Kumar—were passengers in auto-rickshaw DL 1 RM 0893. The driver drove rashly at high speed, causing the auto to collide with a stationary truck (HR 55F 2507) at Wazirabad Road. FIR No. 155/16 was registered under Sections 279/337/338 IPC. Negligence was established via FIR, site plan, and MLC records; respondents produced no controverting witnesses. For DAR 153/16 (Raju Gupta): a disability certificate established 37% physical disability in left lower limb and right upper limb; the Tribunal assessed 20% functional disability following Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343. Income was assessed at minimum wages for unskilled workman (Rs. 9,178 per month as of 15.02.2016); no future prospects were added per Pranay Sethi. Future loss of earnings was Rs. 3,52,432 (income × 12 × multiplier 16 × 20%), with additional awards for wages (5 months), pain and suffering, amenities, medical bills, conveyance, and attendant charges totalling Rs. 5,33,033. Neelam (154/16) and Satish Kumar (155/16) sustained simple injuries and were awarded Rs. 15,000 each. National Insurance Co. held liable for all three awards with 9% interest per annum from date of filing.
